# iliad-135 — new renderings (21.298–399)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| κυλλοπόδιον (Hera to Hephaestus, 21.331; κυλλός "bent, crooked" + πούς) | "bent-footed one" | "bent-footed one" | "club-foot", "lame one", "limping" (each adds a modern or a medical reading), "crooked-foot"; the note says the god is lame |
| ῥινοτόρος (Ἄρης, 21.391; ῥινός "hide" + a root "pierce") | "hide-piercing" | "the hide-piercer" (+ note: usual explanation, not certain) | "shield-piercer", "shield-breaking", "bull-hide-piercing" (each decides what ῥινός is) |
| κυνάμυια (vocative, Ares to Athena, 21.394; κύων "dog" + μυῖα "fly") | "dog-fly" | "dog-fly" | "shameless fly", "bitch", "impudent creature" (each translates the insult instead of the word) |
| θάρσος ἄητον (21.395; ἄητον rare, sense not secure) | "insatiable boldness" | "insatiable boldness" (+ note: one old guess, not secure) | "unapproachable", "terrible", "unbearable" (each decides the open question); kept apart from ἆτος "insatiate" (Ἄρης ἆτος πολέμοιο, 5.388) |
| πανόψιον ἔγχος (21.397; sense disputed: "seen by all" or "all-seeing") | "a spear for all to see" | "a spear for all to see" (+ note: sense disputed) | "all-seeing spear", "conspicuous spear" (reserved for ἀριδείκετος), "spear in full view" |
| ἀλλ’ ἐπάμυνε τάχιστα (21.311, 21.333; same words in the river’s and in Hera’s mouth) | "But come to the defence very quickly" | "But come to the defence very quickly" | "But help very quickly" (the first draft: "help" is kept for ἀρήγω), "come to our aid at once", "ward off" (ἀμύνω); follows the table’s ἐπαμύνω "come to the defence" (5.685, 6.361, 8.414); τάχιστα "very quickly" |
| ἀλέξω (μή ποτ’ ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀλεξήσειν κακὸν ἦμαρ, 21.374) | "ward off" | "ward off" | "keep off", "keep away" (the first draft; the table’s ἀλεξήσεις 9.251 lists "keep away" as avoided), "avert", "defend"; follows the table’s ἀλεξήσεις "you will ward off" (9.251) and the glossary’s "ward off, keep off". The table is not consistent: 13.475 and 21.138 reserve "ward off" for ἀμύνω; the nearest precedent, the same verb and tense, decides |
| κακὸν ἦμαρ (21.374) | "the evil day" | "the evil day" | "day of doom", "day of ruin" (decide for the reader) |
| αὐτίκα δ’ Ἥφαιστον προσεφώνεεν ὃν φίλον υἱόν (21.330; 21.378 αὐτίκ’ ἄρ’ …, whole-line speech introduction) | "and at once she addressed Hephaestus, her own dear son:" · "at once then she addressed Hephaestus, her own dear son:" | "and at once she spoke to Hephaestus, her own dear son:" · "… at once she spoke to Hephaestus, her own dear son:" | "his dear son" (ὅν is the possessive and Hera is the subject); follows the table’s ἡ δ’ αὖ Τηλέμαχον προσεφώνεεν, ὃν φίλον υἱόν (Odyssey 18.214) |
| αὐτὰρ ὅ γ’ Ἥρην πολλὰ λισσόμενος ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (21.367–368) | "But he, to Hera / much entreating, winged words spoke:" | "But he spoke winged words to Hera, entreating her much:" | "begging", "beseeching"; follows the table’s καί μιν λισσόμενος ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (22.311) |
| αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ τό γ’ ἄκουσε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη (21.377) | "But when that she heard, the goddess, white-armed Hera," | "But when the goddess, white-armed Hera, heard that," | "heard this", "heard these words"; the epithet is kept every time as in 1.595 and 8.350 |
| ὣς ἔφαθ’, Ἥφαιστος δὲ τιτύσκετο / κατέσβεσε θεσπιδαὲς πῦρ (21.342, 21.381; the second line only is shared) | "So she spoke, and Hephaestus made ready / quenched the wondrous-blazing fire," | "So she spoke, and Hephaestus made ready / put out his wondrous-blazing fire," | "divinely-blazing"; θεσπιδαὲς πῦρ "wondrous-blazing fire" as in the table (12.441); τιτύσκετο "made ready" as in the table (8.41) |
| πολυμήτιος Ἡφαίστοιο (21.355) | "many-wiled Hephaestus" | "Hephaestus of many wiles" | "of many counsels" (reserved for πολύφρων); follows πολύμητις "many-wiled" / "of many wiles" (Odyssey table), now given to Hephaestus |
| πολύφρονος Ἡφαίστοιο (21.367) | "of Hephaestus, much-minded" | "Hephaestus of the many counsels" | "many-wiled" (reserved for πολύμητις), "wise-hearted" (δαΐφρων); follows the table’s πολύφρων row ("much-minded" / "of the many counsels"), now given to Hephaestus |
| ἲς ποταμοῖο (21.356; ἲς "force", periphrasis for the river) | "the force of the river" | "the river’s force" | "might" (βίη, μένος), "strength" (σθένος), "the river’s fury"; follows the table’s ἲς "force" (11.668, 17.739) |
| ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν (21.356) | "and he spoke a word and called him by name:" | "and he spoke, calling him by name:" | table, unchanged (4.610, 15.552) |
| ἄσις (ἄσιν … καλύψω, 21.321; rare) | "slime" | "slime" | "silt", "mud", "ooze" (decide the kind of deposit); the note gives the usual sense "slime, mud" |
| χέραδος (21.319) | "gravel" | "gravel" | "shingle", "rubble", "stones"; stones are λᾶες (21.314) |
| λέβης (21.362) | "cauldron" | "cauldron" | "pot", "kettle", "bowl" |
| ἁπαλοτρεφέος σιάλοιο (21.363) | "a tender-fed pig" | "a tender-fed pig" | "fatted hog", "well-fed boar" (both turn ἁπαλο- "tender" into "fat") |
| κυκώμενος ὑψόσε θύων (21.324) | "churning, raging high" | "churning and raging high" | "boiling", "seething"; follows κυκώμενος "churning" (21.235), θύω "rage" (the table’s 12.400) |
| κῦμα ῥόοιο … κόρυσσε (21.306) | "armed the wave of his stream" | "armed the wave of his stream" | "raised to a crest", "reared" (the table’s κορύσσεται, 4.424, lists "raises a crest" as avoided), "helmeted"; follows κορύσσω "arm" (4.424, 2.273); the note gives the helmet-image |
| σάλπιγξεν (21.388) | "sounded like a trumpet" | "rang like a trumpet" | "blared", "resounded" (kept for βράχε "resounded", 21.387) |
| ἀθάνατον θεόν (the river, 21.380) | "an immortal god" | "an immortal god" | "deathless god"; keeps the table’s ἀθάνατος "immortal" |
| χώετο, χωομένη περ (21.305, 21.384) | "was incensed", "though incensed" | "was incensed", "incensed though she was" | "raged", "enraged", "angry"; follows the table’s χώομαι "be incensed" (1.44, 4.357) |
| κατὰ μόθον (21.310) | "in the fray" | "in the fray" | "in the tumult"; follows the table’s μόθος "fray" (7.117) |
| ὃς δὴ νῦν κρατέει (21.315) | "who now prevails" | "who is now prevailing" | "has the mastery", "is master"; follows the table’s κρατέω "prevail" (5.175) |
| στυφελίζειν (21.380) | "to thrust roughly" | "to shove" | "buffet", "batter"; follows the table’s στυφελίζω (7.261, 16.703) |
| ἀνῆκεν, ἀνῆκας (21.395, 21.396) | "urge on" | "urge on" | "set on"; follows the table’s ἀνίημι "urge on" with an infinitive or person (5.405, 6.256, 10.389) |
| δαὶ κταμένων αἰζηῶν (21.301; two words in the edition) | "of young men slain in battle" | "from young men slain in battle" | "cut down" (that is δαΐζω in the one-word δαϊκταμένων of 21.146, where the table says "cut down"); here the edition divides the word and the note says δαί "in battle" + κταμένων "slain", so the two words are both kept |

Departures from the Odyssey: none.

Departures from the house table: none, after the reviewer’s pass 1 and 2. The first draft departed from it at ἐπάμυνε ("help"), κόρυσσε ("raised to a crest"), ἀλέξω ("keep away"), χώομαι, μόθος, κρατέω, στυφελίζω and ἀνίημι; the rows above give the table’s rendering. Where an earlier row is reused unchanged (ἀκάματον πῦρ "untiring fire", ὀπωρινὸς Βορέης "the late-summer North Wind", ἀργεστᾶο Νότοιο "of the bright South Wind", διιπετέος ποταμοῖο "the Zeus-fallen river", ποταμὸς βαθυδίνης, κέκλετ’ ἀΰσας "shouted orders to", ἀγακλεές "very famous", ἐρύκακε "held back"), it is not listed again.
